Kuvitus: laboratorion pöydällä on vanhan: Illustration: on a laboratory table is an old-fashioned balance. In the left pan, which is lower, two red protons and two grey neutrons lie apart. In the right pan, which is higher, the same four particles are packed tightly together as a helium nucleus, which glows and sends out two orange photons. The separate particles weigh more than the nucleus assembled from them.
Pylväskuva, pystyakseli mittakaavassa mu: Bar chart, the vertical axis to scale but broken: it starts at the value 3.990 u, not at zero. The left bar is the total mass of two hydrogen atoms and two neutrons, 4.032980 u. The right bar is the mass of a helium-4 atom, 4.002603 u. The difference between the bars, the mass defect, is 0.030377 u, and it is marked with a red bracket.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: energiataso: Diagram, not to scale: energy levels. The upper horizontal line is the energy of separate protons and neutrons: on it are two red protons and two grey neutrons apart. The lower horizontal line is the energy of the helium-4 nucleus: on it the same four nucleons tightly together. On the left an orange arrow pointing up: breaking the nucleus into nucleons requires the binding energy E B. On the right an orange arrow pointing down: when the nucleus forms, the same energy is released. Between the levels is written E B = Δm c².
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: sidosenergia nukl: Graph to scale: binding energy per nucleon in megaelectronvolts as a function of the mass number A, A from zero to 250, the vertical axis from zero to 10 megaelectronvolts. The points are values for 32 nuclei calculated from atomic masses. For deuterium the value is 1.11 MeV, for helium-4 7.07 MeV, clearly higher than its neighbours. The value rises steeply for light nuclei, is highest, about 8.8 MeV, at iron-56 and nickel-62, and falls gently towards heavy nuclei: for uranium-238 7.57 MeV. On the left an orange arrow pointing up and to the right: fusion, the joining of light nuclei. On the right an orange arrow pointing left towards the peak: fission, the splitting of a heavy nucleus.
Pylväskuva, pystyakseli mittakaavassa mu: Bar chart, the vertical axis to scale but broken: it starts at the value 238.040 u, not at zero. The left bar is the mass of a uranium-238 atom, 238.050787 u. The right bar is the combined mass of the thorium-234 and helium-4 atoms formed in alpha decay, 238.046204 u. The difference 0.004583 u is marked with a red bracket, and it corresponds to the reaction energy Q = 4.27 MeV.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: sidosenergia nukl: Graph to scale: binding energy per nucleon in megaelectronvolts as a function of the mass number A, A from zero to 250, the vertical axis from zero to 10 megaelectronvolts. The points are values for 32 nuclei calculated from atomic masses: the value rises steeply for light nuclei, is highest, about 8.8 MeV, when A is about 60, and falls gently to 7.6 MeV when A is about 240. Readings: when A is about 30, the value is about 8.5 MeV; when A is about 60, about 8.8 MeV; when A is about 120, about 8.5 MeV; when A is about 240, about 7.6 MeV. The names of the nuclei and the reactions are not marked in the picture.
